newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING says ex-client loses Dutch court action.
newsitem.headline: ING says ex-client loses Dutch court action.

text.p: Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING) said on Thursday a Dutch court had rejected a businessman's application for an injunction forcing ING to sell him back the business he founded.
An ING spokesman said the Amsterdam District Court denied the application by Joost Ritman, who wanted ING to sell him De Ster, a disposable plates and cutlery firm, for Dfl 375 million.
ING took control of De Ster in 1993 after Ritman failed to meet debt repayments.
Ritman's lawyer Peter Wakkie said his client would appeal within 14 days.
Ritman claims that under an agreement with ING, he has the right to match any third party bid for the company.
ING and Ritman disputed in court whether ING's negotiations with Bahrein-based investment company Investcorp late last year and earlier this year constituted a bid for De Ster.
But Wakkie said Ritman believed evidence should have convinced the court the talks were at a sufficiently advanced stage to trigger Ritman's right to make a counter offer.
